Agropoli (port locode ITAGP) is port city in Salerno province, Campania region (Italy). it is located at the beginning of Cilento coast on Tyrrhenian Sea.

Agropoli is an important access port to nearby ancient site of Paestum. Established by the Greeks in 600 BC, the well-preserved site was rediscovered in 1752. Today it features the impressive Amphitheatre, Athenian Basilica, and the Temple of Poseidon.

Founded by the Byzantines in the 6th century, Agropoli boasts a medieval old town that has remained intact, together with surrounding defensive walls, and a 7th-century entrance gate. Angevin-Aragonese castle, built on 6th-century Byzantine foundations, stands on top of a promontory. There is another promontory to the west of the modern tourist harbour, on which the 16th-century coastal tower of San Francesco stands next to the remains of a convent of the same name.

Other main sights in Agripoli include tombs predating the Byzantine period and 16th-century Churches of Holy Mary of Constantinople, San Marco, and San Francesco. Trentova Bay beaches contribute to making the city an important seaside resort. The Municipal Antiquarian presents a collection of archaeological finds.

Agropoli is a compact Cilento port where the medieval old town, castle and waterfront are practical to explore independently. Cruise ships generally anchor offshore rather than berth inside the shallow tourist harbour, so passengers should expect tender operations. The major excursion from Agropoli is Paestum, one of Italy's best-preserved Greek archaeological sites.

At a Glance

  • Agropoli town: Easy independently, although the historic center and castle require a steep climb and stairs.
  • Cruise access: Ships normally anchor in the roadstead and transfer passengers ashore by tender. Follow the ship's instructions for the exact landing point and last tender time.
  • Old town: About 10 minutes on foot from the harbour area.
  • Castle: About 15 minutes on foot, including an uphill section.
  • Agropoli-Castellabate railway station: About 1.9 km (1.2 mi) from the port.
  • Paestum: Roughly 12–14 km (7.5–8.7 mi) away; independent travel is practical with advance transport planning.

Getting from the Cruise Port

Agropoli's harbour is primarily a marina for yachts and smaller craft, with limited depth for cruise vessels. Cruise calls therefore normally use an offshore anchorage and tenders to bring passengers into the harbour area.

Once ashore, no transfer is needed for central Agropoli. The medieval quarter is less than a 10-minute walk away via the waterfront and the streets below the promontory. Taxis are available locally and are useful for Paestum or for passengers who want to avoid longer walks.

The railway station is about 1.9 km (1.2 mi) from the port, making the train possible for Paestum, but the extra walk or taxi transfer to the station needs to be included in the schedule.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Explore the Old Town and Castello Angioino-Aragonese

Recommended time: 1.5–2.5 hours. Independent: Easy.

From the harbour, walk toward the base of the old town and climb the Scaloni Ennio Balbo to the historic entrance. Continue through the stone gateway to Piazza Madonna di Costantinopoli, the narrow lanes of the borgo and the castle at the top of the promontory. The principal attraction is as much the setting and coastal views as the individual buildings.

The climb includes steep streets and many steps, so it is less suitable for passengers with limited mobility. Castle access and opening times should be checked on the day of the visit.

Visit Paestum

Recommended time: 4–5 hours including transport. Independent: Practical with planning.

Paestum is the strongest choice for passengers interested in archaeology. Its archaeological area contains three exceptionally well-preserved Greek temples together with Roman remains and a museum.

By road, allow roughly 20–25 minutes each way under normal conditions. A taxi arranged for both directions is the simplest independent option.

Train travel is also possible. Agropoli-Castellabate station is about 1.9 km (1.2 mi) from the port, and direct regional trains can reach Paestum in approximately 6–10 minutes. From Paestum station, the archaeological area and museum are about a 15-minute walk through Porta Sirena. Train frequencies vary, so check the current timetable before leaving the ship and identify a suitable return service in advance.

For a short port call, or when tender and train timings leave little margin, an organized excursion or prearranged taxi is the safer practical choice.

Baia di Trentova

Recommended time: 2.5–4 hours. Independent: Easy with walking or a short taxi ride.

Trentova Bay is the main beach and nature option close to Agropoli. The coastal walk from the port is about 2 km (1.2 mi) each way and takes approximately one hour at a relaxed pace. It follows a paved panoramic road and passes the San Francesco coastal area before reaching the bay.

A taxi is preferable if the objective is simply to spend time swimming rather than use much of the port call walking. Beach facilities are most active in the warmer months.

Waterfront and Lungomare San Marco

Recommended time: 1–2 hours. Independent: Very easy.

Passengers wanting a low-effort visit can remain around the marina, central streets and Lungomare San Marco. This is substantially flatter than the old town and works well for a short call, a meal or a stroll before returning to the tender.

Self-Guided Walking Tours

Historic Agropoli Walk

Distance: about 2–2.5 km (1.2–1.6 mi) round trip. Pure walking time: 35–45 minutes. Recommended total time: 1.5–2 hours. Difficulty: Moderate because of the steep climb and stairs.

  1. Harbour area: Start where the tender transfer brings passengers ashore and walk along the waterfront toward the historic center.
  2. Via Cavour and Via Rupe: Continue toward the foot of the old-town promontory.
  3. Scaloni Ennio Balbo: Climb the broad staircase leading to the historic entrance.
  4. Old-town gateway: Pass through the monumental entrance into the medieval borgo.
  5. Piazza Madonna di Costantinopoli: Stop at the church and viewpoints overlooking the harbour and coast.
  6. Historic lanes: Continue uphill through the compact network of narrow streets.
  7. Castello Angioino-Aragonese: Reach the highest point of the walk for wide coastal views.
  8. Return: Descend through the same old-town entrance and continue back to the harbour.

This route is straightforward without a guide, but comfortable shoes are advisable because of stone paving, stairs and steep gradients.

Port to Trentova Coastal Walk

Distance: about 4 km (2.5 mi) round trip to Trentova Bay. Pure walking time: about 1.5–2 hours. Recommended total time: 3–4 hours with beach time. Difficulty: Easy to moderate.

  1. Start at Agropoli harbour.
  2. Follow the coastal road away from the town center.
  3. Pass the San Francesco coastal area and viewpoints.
  4. Continue along the panoramic road toward Trentova.
  5. Spend time at Baia di Trentova before returning by the same route or taking a taxi back to the harbour.

The route is largely paved but has some gradients and limited shade. In hot summer weather, carrying water and using a taxi for one direction can make the outing considerably easier.

Practical Tips

  • Tendering adds uncertainty to both the start and end of the visit. Base plans on the ship's announced last tender rather than the published departure time.
  • For Paestum, confirm the return train or arrange a return taxi before starting the visit.
  • Allow additional return margin when traveling outside Agropoli; traffic, train delays and tender queues can all affect timing.
  • The old town is compact but steep. Passengers avoiding stairs can enjoy the harbour, modern center and waterfront instead.
  • Summer afternoons can be very hot, particularly on the climb to the castle and on the exposed road toward Trentova.
